LinkedIn generated $17.8 billion in 2025 (specifically $17.812 billion), up from $16.372 billion in 2024. That means LinkedIn revenue grew by about $1.4 billion year-over-year, before reaching $19.8 billion in fiscal 2026.
That revenue comes from three main business lines:
Membership subscriptions: Premium and Sales Navigator plans

Microsoft’s latest quarterly earnings report says LinkedIn revenue increased 12% year-over-year in Q3 2026.

Subscriptions are becoming a bigger part of the story. LinkedIn Premium passed $2 billion in annual revenue for the first time in Q2 2025, a sign that members are paying for better visibility and reach.
4. Daniel Shapero became LinkedIn CEO in April 2026
LinkedIn named Dan Shapero as its new CEO in April 2026. Shapero previously served as LinkedIn’s Chief Operating Officer and has been with the company since 2008.
LinkedIn officially launched on May 5, 2003, just nine months before Facebook launched at Harvard. It was founded by Reid Hoffman.
Microsoft acquired LinkedIn in 2016. Ryan Roslansky led the company through its most recent growth period before Shapero stepped into the CEO role.

LinkedIn earned a customer satisfaction score of 77 out of 100 in the American Customer Satisfaction Index for 2025, beating the overall social media average of 74. It also scored higher than Instagram, Reddit, Snapchat, Facebook, and X.

As of October 2025, 25- to 34-year-olds made up the largest share of LinkedIn users worldwide, at 33.4%. In other words, LinkedIn’s biggest audience segment is made up of older Gen Z and younger Millennials.

Americans are still the most frequent visitors, though. The U.S. accounts for 34% of all LinkedIn web traffic, with India second at 8.25%.

21. LinkedIn accounts with 100K+ followers post 43 times per month

LinkedIn accounts with more than 100,000 followers posted an average of 43.48 times per month as of January 2025. Small accounts (those up to 1,000 followers) posted an average of 9.98 times per month.

If you’re a smaller brand, that gap is less about volume and more about cadence. Big accounts post roughly daily. A smaller team can compete by showing up two or three times a week with content worth reading.
22. Companies that post weekly see a 2x lift in engagement with their content

Companies that post at least once a week see 2x higher engagement with their content, which makes a regular posting schedule one of the easiest wins for brands. Sounds too overwhelming? Start with one strong post per week, then build from there.

24. LinkedIn posts with images see 2x higher comment rates

Organizations looking to get the most engagement from their posts should include an image with each post on LinkedIn. Custom image collages (3-4 images in one post) perform especially well, giving users more visual context and helping expand your reach.

Video is gaining serious momentum on LinkedIn. The platform says video creation increased 27% in 2025, while video views rose 36%. Supply is growing fast, but demand is growing faster.

27. Paid video on LinkedIn grew 25% year-over-year

B2B audiences are engaging with video content on LinkedIn. LinkedIn says paid video ads grew 25% year-over-year, thanks in part to more creator partnerships and better measurement tools for advertisers.
For brands, that means video ads, live video, and other visual-first formats are becoming a bigger part of the LinkedIn marketing mix.
28. Video gets 5x more engagement on LinkedIn
Video is one of the best ways to stop the scroll on LinkedIn. Formats that tend to work well:
Product demos: Show the thing instead of describing it
Expert tips: One useful idea, delivered in under a minute
Customer stories: Let someone else make your case
Behind-the-scenes: Humanize the team and the work
Quick explainers: Break down a complex topic simply
Just remember: LinkedIn users are usually scrolling between meetings, emails, and actual work. Keep videos clear, useful, and easy to understand without sound.

What are the latest LinkedIn statistics marketers need to know?

The LinkedIn statistics that matter most in 2026 start with scale: LinkedIn has more than 1.4 billion members worldwide. It’s also growing as a revenue driver for Microsoft, with LinkedIn generating $17.8 billion in revenue in 2025 and revenue up 12% year-over-year in Q3 2026.
How many people use LinkedIn in 2026?

LinkedIn has more than 1.4 billion registered members worldwide in 2026, and the site draws around 2.1 billion visits per month. Registered members and active users aren’t the same thing, so monthly visits give you a better sense of real activity than total sign-ups.
What LinkedIn demographics and user behavior trends matter most for businesses?

The LinkedIn demographics that matter most are age, geography, and education level. More than 78% of LinkedIn users are outside the U.S., the platform’s largest age group worldwide is 25- to 34-year-olds, and most members hold a bachelor’s degree or higher. That makes LinkedIn a strong place to reach older Gen Z and younger Millennial professionals as they build careers and start influencing buying decisions.
How do LinkedIn engagement and advertising statistics compare to other platforms?

LinkedIn engagement and advertising statistics show higher costs but stronger returns than most other paid social channels. Dreamdata’s benchmark data found the average CPC for LinkedIn ads was about $6.93 USD, while LinkedIn ads delivered 121% ROAS compared to 67% for Google Search and 51% for Meta. The comparison table in our advertising section breaks this down side by side.
How effective are LinkedIn ads compared to other platforms?

LinkedIn ads are more effective than most other platforms for B2B marketers on a return basis, with Dreamdata benchmarks showing 121% ROAS versus 67% for Google Search and 51% for Meta. The trade-off is cost per click, which runs around $6.93 USD on LinkedIn. You pay more per click, but the clicks come from a more qualified professional audience.
What LinkedIn statistics should B2B marketers use to guide strategy?

B2B marketers should build strategy around LinkedIn’s decision-maker audience, ad reach, and sales cycle length. LinkedIn ads can reach 1.55 billion people, the platform includes millions of executives and senior influencers, and Dreamdata found it takes an average of 281 days from first ad impression to revenue. Plan budgets and attribution windows accordingly.
What types of content get the most engagement on LinkedIn?

Video gets the most engagement on LinkedIn, at 5x more engagement than other formats. Posts with images see 2x higher comment rates, and custom image collages of three to four images perform especially well. Posting at least once a week doubles engagement on its own.
How are LinkedIn usage and content trends changing for brands and professionals?

LinkedIn usage is becoming more active and more visual. CEO posting is up 52%, video views are up 36%, and paid video ads grew 25% year-over-year. Brands are also posting more often, with large LinkedIn accounts publishing an average of 43 posts per month.
What is the 3/2/1 rule on LinkedIn?

The 3/2/1 rule on LinkedIn is a content mix framework: For every six posts, share three pieces of industry-relevant content, two “proud” posts celebrating your team or company, and one promotional post. It’s a simple way to keep your feed useful instead of turning your Page into a sales channel.
